title: Continuous matrix detection for locally finite free normed coefficients
statement: Work in compatible small-site and coefficient universes. Let $F$ be a normed field with totally disconnected metric topology, put $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ for profinite $P$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $F_T=p_T^*C_F$ for every scheme $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Modules mean internal $F_T$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with module inverse images as in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Let $T$ be any scheme, and let $M,N$ be $F_T$-modules with finite constant local models [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. For a morphism $h:M\to N$, assume that for every algebraically closed field $k$ and geometric point $y:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the $F$-linear map $\Gamma(s,y^*h)$ is invertible, with scalars given by constant sections. Then $h$ is an isomorphism. More precisely, there is a common pro-etale covering $(U_j\to T)_j$ and finite free models $M|_{U_j}\cong F_{U_j}^{n_j}$, $N|_{U_j}\cong F_{U_j}^{m_j}$. In these models $h|_{U_j}$ is a matrix $A_j$ with entries in $C(|U_j|,F)$, via the canonical coefficient realization. Its pullback to a geometric point over $u\in|U_j|$ is the matrix $A_j(u)$. For each nonempty $U_j$ one has $m_j=n_j$ and $\det A_j(u)\ne0$ for every $u$; the continuous matrix $u\mapsto(\det A_j(u))^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(A_j(u))$ defines an inverse to $h|_{U_j}$ compatible with restriction to every pro-etale object over $U_j$. Empty covering members impose no rank equality. No Noetherianity or stratification of $T$, and no completeness of $F$, is assumed.

source.place: Example 3.1 and Section 3; agent continuous determinant/adjugate and covering descent argument (old step 6).

proof.text: Choose the finite constant models of $M,N$. Their scalar ring is $C_F(*)=F$. The field clause of the scalar finite-basis lemma gives bases of every finitely presented model. The finite-power scalar-extension identifications therefore give finite free models. Refine the two covers by their fibre products; base change and composition of coverings give a common pro-etale cover. Restriction to a slice is sectionwise, so the specified bases restrict to bases on this refinement. The weakly etale localization identifies its slice site with the small site of each $U_j$. For the underlying abelian sheaves inverse image along an object of the site is restriction. Under continuous coefficient realization both restricted and intrinsic coefficient rings have sections $C(|V|,F)$ on $V\to U_j$; their comparison is the identity there, by the normalized precomposition formula. Thus the ringed module inverse image in the statement agrees with these restrictions.

source.place: Example 3.1 and Remark 3.2, p.6; agent finite-free matrix proof and cover descent (Stacks sites.tex Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, for the final gluing).

proof.text: Use the internal/sectionwise module equivalence to read sections without changing them. Continuous coefficient realization is compatible with the ring operations: its naturality for continuous addition and multiplication, and its finite-product and unit compatibility, identify the pulled-back ring with the pointwise function ring. The finite-free Hom bijection now assigns to $h|_{U_j}$ a unique $m_j\times n_j$ matrix $A_j$ in $C(|U_j|,F)$. On $v:V\to U_j$ it acts by $b\mapsto A_j\circ|v|\,b$, since its entries are the images of the global basis sections and restriction is precomposition.

source.place: Example 3.1 and Remark 3.2, p.6; agent finite-free matrix proof and cover descent (Stacks sites.tex Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, for the final gluing).

proof.text: Let $z:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to U_j$ be a geometric point with image $u$, and put $y=(U_j\to T)z$. Module pullback is additive and preserves finite biproducts. In the resulting coordinates $z^*F_{U_j}^{r}\cong F_s^{r}$, each matrix entry pulls back to the constant $a_{ab}(u)$: the normalized coefficient adjunct is precomposition, and $|s|$ is a singleton. One can check this on $a_{ab}e_b$; functoriality and the finite biproduct identities then give all entries. Thus $\Gamma(s,z^*(h|_{U_j}))$ has matrix $A_j(u)$ over $\Gamma(s,F_s)=C(|s|,F)=F$. The inverse-image composition isomorphism identifies it with $\Gamma(s,y^*h)$, so it is invertible by hypothesis.

source.place: Example 3.1 and Remark 3.2, p.6; agent finite-free matrix proof and cover descent (Stacks sites.tex Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, for the final gluing).

proof.text: For every $u\in|U_j|$, choose an algebraic closure $k$ of its residue field; the canonical $\operatorname{Spec}k\to U_j$ is a geometric point above $u$. Step 3 gives an invertible $F$-linear map $F^{n_j}\to F^{m_j}$. The image of its standard basis is a basis, so invariance of finite basis cardinality gives $m_j=n_j$ whenever $U_j$ is nonempty. After this identification, the determinant criterion gives $\det A_j(u)\ne0$ for every $u$. No geometric-point lifting through a cover is needed: we choose the geometric point on $U_j$ itself.

source.place: Example 3.1 and Remark 3.2, p.6; agent finite-free matrix proof and cover descent (Stacks sites.tex Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, for the final gluing).

proof.text: For a nonempty $U_j$ apply the continuous adjugate inverse lemma to $X=|U_j|$ and $A_j$. It gives the continuous matrix $B_j(u)=(\det A_j(u))^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(A_j(u))$ with $A_jB_j=B_jA_j=I$. The Hom bijection turns $B_j$ into a morphism inverse to $h|_{U_j}$. On any $v:V\to U_j$ the matrix is $B_j\circ|v|$; substitution in both identities proves the two inverse identities on every section over $V$. This proves the requested restriction compatibility. If $n_j=0$, the determinant is $1$ and the matrices are empty. If $U_j$ is empty, every section group is zero by the sheaf condition for the empty covering, so the unique map between the two restricted modules is invertible even if their displayed ranks differ.

source.place: Example 3.1 and Remark 3.2, p.6; agent finite-free matrix proof and cover descent (Stacks sites.tex Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, for the final gluing).

proof.text: The local inverses agree on overlaps: both are two-sided inverses to the restriction of $h$, and $g_1=g_1(hg_2)=(g_1h)g_2=g_2$. Apply the map-gluing clause of set-sheaf cover descent to their underlying sheaf maps. The glued map $g:N\to M$ is additive and $F_T$-linear because the two equations for additivity and scalar multiplication hold after restriction to the cover and equality of sections is local. The identities $gh=1$ and $hg=1$ hold for the same reason. Transport $g$ back through the internal/sectionwise equivalence. This is the inverse of $h$. For empty $T$ the empty covering gives zero sheaves and the same conclusion.

This is the first split of a node Q33 created on 2026-10-22; it had no earlier proof and has no repair note, so it is not a re-split. The statement is unchanged. Tested cases: empty T or empty U_j (no rank equality), rank 0 (det 1), a rank-1 non-constant unit 1/a, and m≠n (impossible at a geometric point). Step 1: the local-model scalar ring is C(*,F)=F, so the field clause of the scalar finite-free node gives a basis, and the flatness-free clause of constant-finite-free-presentation-extension gives free models. Only clause 1 (sets, abelian groups, rings) of proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction is used. alpha_f in sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms is the point-pullback composition comparison, so the coherence node reduces module pullback to restriction. Step 2: realization gives sections C(|V|,F) as a ring isomorphism, and the ringed-site matrix node gives the Hom/matrix bijection, composition to product and the sectionwise action. Step 3: additivity, transported biproduct maps, the adjunct being precomposition (a(u) on the one-point |s|) and the composition isomorphism. Step 4: algebraic closure of κ(u) gives a geometric point on U_j itself; basis cardinality gives m=n; the det criterion follows. Step 5: the new leaf applied on |U_j|. Step 6: map gluing plus a local linearity check. proof_deps equal the union of uses; no cycle (closure of 641 nodes); no SGA.
